questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The airhostess said to the passengers, “This is our inaugural flight starting today.”

options.text: The airhostess informed the passengers that it was their inaugural flight starting today.
The airhostess told to the passengers that it was their inaugural flight starting that day.
The airhostess said to the passengers that this is our inaugural flight starting today.
The airhostess informed the passengers that it was their inaugural flight starting that day.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the direct speech is converted into indirect speech.
 
• The pronoun "this" is changed to "that" and the phrase "starting today" is changed to "starting that day".
 
• Reported speech is used to tell someone what another person said without quoting the exact words.
 
• The verb "said" is often changed to "informed" or "told" in indirect speech.

Hence, the correct indirect speech is *'**The airhostess informed the passengers that it was their inaugural flight starting that day*****.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When converting direct speech to indirect speech, it is important to change the tense, pronouns, and time expressions accordingly.
 
• Example: *Direct: She said, **"I am going to the market today."***

 *Indirect: **She said that she was going to the market that day.***

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

He said to me, “ I have done my duty.”

options.text: He told me that I had done my duty.
He told me that he had done his duty.
He told me that he have done his duty.
He told me that he did his duty.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the **past perfect tense**, and the correct auxiliary verb to use is 'had'.As in indirect speech Present perfect tense changes into Past perfect tense.
 
• The pronoun '**I' **changes to **'he'** in the indirect form.
 
• The **possessive adjective** **'my'** changes to **'his**' in the indirect form.
 
• The reporting verb '**said to**' changes to **'told' **when converting to indirect speech.

 

Hence, the correct indirect form is** '*He told me that he had done his duty*.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Ensure the reporting verb is correctly modified according to the context of the sentence.
 
 
• **Example:** Direct: **She said to him, "I am happy."** Indirect:** She told him that she was happy.**

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The teacher said to Kavya, “You need a new notebook for English.”

options.text: The teacher told to Kavya that she needs a new notebook for English.
The teacher told Kavya that she needed a new notebook for English.
The teacher told Kavya that you needed a new notebook for English.
The teacher said to Kavya that you need a new notebook for English.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In indirect speech, the** pronoun **and **tense** often change to maintain the original meaning.
 
• The pronoun **"you**" changes to "**she**" when referring to Kavya.
 
• The present tense "need" changes to the past tense "needed" in indirect speech.
 
• Therefore, "The teacher told Kavya that she needed a new notebook for English" is the correct indirect form.

Hence, the correct indirect form is '***The teacher told Kavya that she needed a new notebook for English*.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When converting direct speech to indirect speech, personal pronouns and tense usually need to be adjusted.
 
• For example, if the reporting verb is in the past tense, the verb in the reported speech typically shifts one tense back.
 
• Pronouns are changed to match the subject of the reporting verb.
 
• Example:
 
 
• Direct:** He said, "I am tired."**
 
• Indirect:** He said that he was tired.**

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

You said, “ Priya kept watching television till her mother exploded at her.”

options.text: You said that Priya kept watching television till her mother exploded at her.
You said that Priya had kept watching television till her mother exploded at her.
You said that Priya kept watching television till her mother had exploded at her.
You said that Priya had kept watching television till her mother had exploded at her.

questions.solution:
The correct option is: **1) You said that Priya kept watching television till her mother exploded at her.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence involves a **time clause** ("till her mother exploded at her"), which is used to describe when the action of "watching television" ended.
 
• The use of the word **"till"** indicates a specific point in time when the action of watching television stopped, making it a time clause. 
 
• In indirect speech, when the reporting verb is in the past tense (like "said"), the action in the direct speech is generally shifted to the past tense.
 
• In this case, since the action of watching television is continuous up until a specific point in time (when the mother exploded), the past simple tense "kept" remains appropriate, and the time clause "till her mother exploded" is in the past simple as well.

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***You said that Priya kept watching television till her mother exploded at her.***

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

She held the child’s hand firmly.

options.text: The child’s hand is held firmly.
The child’s hand has been held firmly.
The child’s hand held firmly.
The child’s hand was held firmly.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'The child’s hand was held firmly'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the past tense: "She held the child’s hand firmly."
 
• To convert it to passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The verb "held" in the past tense must be converted to the passive form "was held."
 
• The agent (the doer of the action) in the active sentence ("She") is either omitted or included at the end in a passive sentence, but "firmly" remains in place to describe how the action was done.
 
• The structure of the correct passive form maintains the past tense: "The child’s hand was held firmly."
 
• "The child’s hand" now acts as the subject, and "was held" is the past passive construction of the verb.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 (The child’s hand is held firmly): Incorrect because it is in the present tense.
 
• Option 2 (The child’s hand has been held firmly): Incorrect because it is in the present perfect tense.
 
• Option 3 (The child’s hand held firmly): Incorrect because it lacks the auxiliary verb needed for the passive voice.

• The direct speech sentence is a question and is converted into indirect speech by changing the question form to a statement form.
 
• The reporting verb '**said to'** is changed into **'asked'** because it is a question.
 
• The conjunction** 'if' **is used to connect the reported speech.

He told me that I am going to France the following week.
He said to me that he were going to France next week.
He told me that he was going to France the following week.

__
 
• The** direct speech** in the sentence uses the present continuous tense "**am going"**, which should be changed to the past continuous tense **"was going"** in the **indirect speech.**
 
• The time expression "**next week**" in direct speech should be changed to "**the following week"** in indirect speech.
 
• The reporting verb **"said to"** is usually changed to "**told**" when converting to indirect speech.

Hence, the correct statement is '***He told me that he was going to France the following week***.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When converting direct speech to indirect speech, the pronoun "**I**" changes to "**he" or "she" **depending on the subject of the reporting clause.

 
 
• **Example:** *She said, "**I am going to the market."*** changes to *She said that **she was going to the market.***
 
 
 
• Time expressions in direct speech are often changed in indirect speech.
 
 
• Example: *"**today" changes to "that day",** "**tomorrow" changes to "the next day"**, "**yesterday" changes to "the previous day",** etc.*

questions.question:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.

She exclaimed with regret that she had acted very foolishly

options.text: “Ah! Have I acted foolishly?” she said.
“I have acted foolishly,” she said.
“Alas! How foolishly I have acted,” she said.
“Oh! I regret having acted foolishly,” she said.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an** indirect speech** that needs to be converted to **direct speech.**
 
• In direct speech, the actual words of the speaker** are quoted.**
 
• The sentence is an exclamatory sentence. So word like 'Alas' is perfect to express the grief or regret of the narrator.
 
• Expressions of emotions like **"exclaimed with regret"** can be translated to words like** "Alas!" in direct speech**.
 
 
• **Example:** *She **exclaimed with regret** that she had acted very foolishly.* becomes *“**Alas! How foolishly I have acted,” **__she said.*
 
 

Therefore the correct statement is** *****“Alas! How foolishly I have acted,” she said.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Direct speech involves quoting the exact words spoken by the speaker.
 
• Indirect speech involves reporting the words spoken by the speaker without quoting them exactly.
 
• In direct speech, emotional expressions can be translated using appropriate interjections like **"Alas!" **for **regret**, **"Oh!"** for **surprise, **etc.
 
 
• **Example:** *“Oh! I regret having acted foolishly,” she said.* can also be a correct transformation but does not capture the same level of regret as "Alas!".

questions.question:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.

The old man prayed to God to help him in his hour of sorrow.

options.text: The old man said, “ O God, help me in my hour of sorrow.”
The old man said, “ God must help him in his hour of sorrow.”
The old man said, “ O God, help him in my hour of sorrow.”
The old man said, “ O God, help me in his hour of sorrow.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the old man is praying to God, which is a direct appeal.
 
• The direct form of the sentence should preserve the exact words spoken by the old man.
 
• Option 1 correctly reflects the direct speech by using quotation marks and the exact words spoken by the old man.
 
• Other options either alter the pronouns or the structure of the original sentence, making them incorrect.

Hence, the correct statement is **'*The old man said, “O God, help me in my hour of sorrow.”*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Direct speech involves quoting the exact words spoken by someone, enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Indirect speech, on the other hand, involves paraphrasing the spoken words without using quotation marks and often involves changes in pronouns and verb tenses.
 
• It is important to maintain the original meaning and context when converting from indirect to direct speech.

__
 
• In the given sentence, the verb tense is in the** present,** and the **pronoun usage needs to be consistent with the subject.**
